artifact.summary:
SEED OUTCOME: the app itself holds your 2023 and 2024 expense records, so those years are visible alongside day-to-day logging instead of living only in Google Sheets. Feasibility is judged and reported before any write is attempted.

INCLUDED SCOPE: 2023 and 2024 only. A written feasibility verdict first — possible, possible-with-caveats, or not possible, with the reason. If feasible: those records land in the app with correct categories, dates, and amounts; existing data is proven intact by a before/after check rather than asserted; and an exercised undo path exists.

EXCLUDED SCOPE: all other archive years, which 060 inventories and analyses; the growth analysis itself; any new app UI for browsing historical years; and any change to how the app treats categories going forward beyond what landing these two years requires.

PROOF NEEDED TO DECIDE WHETHER SPECCING SHOULD START — the questions spec must answer:
- Whether 2023 data exists, settled by inspecting tab gid=0.
- A decision surface for the 25-bucket to flat-gov_category mismatch, raised to the captain rather than resolved by the implementer.
- A ruling on rental-property pass-through and income rows, which distort every total the app shows if imported silently.
- The aggregate-row filter: section totals and per-kind subtotals sit interleaved with real line items, so importing them double-counts. The row-kind tag in column A is the filter.
- The per-year source-file pick rule, where duplicate, template, and legacy .xls variants exist.
- The undo and blast-radius plan, including whether the run happens against staging first.

DEPENDENCY: this feature blocks 060-historical-expense-analysis. You chose migration-first, so the 2006-2025 growth report is specced after this lands and may read the migrated data as a source.
